rationale: Complete bounded review of this exact public MIT source commit scanned every distributable source file and found no protected DSH mutation, dynamic module loading, native executable artifact, lifecycle hook, or runtime dependency. The sole scanner self-match is the child_process detector regex in src/automation-source-policy.mjs and is hash-bound as a false positive. The remaining child-process warnings are actual execFile/spawn calls for the official DSH CLI, Node, and macOS launchctl, all using argument arrays without shell evaluation; these are retained as restricted command capability. The actual package writes manager-owned Profile Patch data, local operation/recovery files, and logs; it makes outbound requests to configured service endpoints, including user-configurable model URLs; and it handles API keys and DSH web-session tokens. These are accurately disclosed as high risk, file write, network any, restricted commands, and API-key/web-session-token credentials. This is an owner-authorized fixed-source review, not an independent security audit or real DSH/Profile acceptance.

findingReviews.rationale: This match is a regular-expression detector for the text child_process; this module does not launch a child process. The finding is an exact scanner self-match and is bound to this file hash.
The module invokes the configured DSH CLI through execFile with an argument vector; it does not compose a shell command. The process boundary is intentionally declared as restricted commands.
Guardian starts the official DSH CLI and Node processes with explicit argv arrays and shell:false; paths and profile operations are validated against the typed plan.
Guardian upgrade and recovery invoke launchctl through execFile with fixed operation verbs and validated path arguments; no shell command string is evaluated.
Guardian invokes launchctl through execFile argument arrays to inspect or stop only its owned service; no shell command string is evaluated.
Legacy repair invokes the official DSH CLI through execFile with bounded arguments and a restricted environment; no shell command string is evaluated.
